A 22-year-old male presents with a 2-day history of neck pain that began after playing a prolonged
tennis match. He denies experiencing any numbness or tingling. On physical examination, no
neurological deficits are noted, and C4 shows resistance to right translation, which improves with
backward bending of the head. The patient agrees to osteopathic manipulative treatment using the Still
technique. When treating this patient's C4 somatic dysfunction with the Still technique, the initial
positioning of C4 should be in Answer Choices: (A) flexion with left sidebending and right rotation (B)
extension with left sidebending and right rotation (C) flexion with right sidebending and left rotation (D)
extension with right sidebending and right rotation (E) neutral with left sidebending and left rotation (F)
flexion with right sidebending and right rotation (G) neutral with right sidebending and right rotation (H)
extension with right sidebending and left rotation (I) flexion with left sidebending and left rotation (J)
extension with left sidebending and left rotation
 A. flexion with left sidebending and left rotation
B. extension with left sidebending and right rotation
C. neutral with right sidebending and right rotation

D. extension with left sidebending and left rotation
E. extension with right sidebending and right rotation
F. flexion with right sidebending and left rotation
G. neutral with left sidebending and left rotation
H. extension with right sidebending and left rotation
I. flexion with left sidebending and right rotation
J. flexion with right sidebending and right rotation
